transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel like I’m constantly bracing myself—my whole body stays tight all day from worrying about my husband and everything I’m juggling. My primary care doctor actually noticed how tense I was during a routine visit and suggested I seek care because this strain has become so overwhelming.
Can you tell me more about what's causing you to worry, is it a specific stressful event or situation that's been ongoing, or more of a general feeling of anxiety?

It really started about nine months ago when my husband was diagnosed with diabetes and heart failure, and I took on all of his care. But now, it has snowballed into a constant, general anxiety where my mind constantly jumps from his health to my community commitments and endless "what-ifs." I just feel like I'm always juggling everything and bracing for the next thing to go wrong.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain activities, places, or social situations because of your anxiety or fear of something going wrong?

Yes, I've started skipping or leaving early from my book club and art center planning sessions because I'm just too wound up and distracted to follow the conversations. Even at home, I'm falling behind on basic chores like laundry and paying bills because so much of my energy goes into worrying.
Can you describe a recent situation where you felt overwhelmed by anxiety, and was it triggered by a specific thought, event, or the anticipation of a potential problem?

Just the other night, I was trying to read for my book club, but my mind kept spinning with "what-ifs" about my husband's heart and blood sugar. Then my phone buzzed with a text from his clinic, and I jumped out of my skin, immediately panicking that some disaster was happening. It takes almost nothing to set me on edge like that.
Have you experienced any panic attacks, where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, and included symptoms like palpitations, sweating, or shortness of breath?
No, I haven't had those sudden panic attacks with sweating or shortness of breath. For me, it's more of a constant, steady state of worry and physical tension that just stays with me all day long.
Can you tell me more about how your avoidance of certain activities or situations has affected your daily life and relationships?

Skipping my book club and the art center planning has really strained my relationships, as I feel too distracted to follow conversations and worry I'm letting everyone down. At home, falling behind on basic chores like laundry and paying bills on time just makes my daily life feel completely overwhelming, leaving me with no energy to enjoy my retirement.
Was there a specific event or situation that triggered the start of your constant worrying and anxiety, or did it gradually build up over time without a clear starting point?

It was triggered about nine months ago when my husband was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and heart failure, and I suddenly had to manage all his medications, diet, and appointments. Balancing those new caregiving duties with my community commitments caused the anxiety to gradually build up over the next couple of months. Since then, it has become a constant, daily struggle for the past seven months.
Do you find yourself persistently replaying or ruminating on the worst-case scenarios or 'what-ifs' related to your husband's health or other areas of your life?

Yes, I constantly struggle with persistent "what-ifs" and worst-case scenarios that I just can't seem to control. Even when I tell myself to stop, thoughts about my husband's heart, his blood sugar, or letting people down at the art center barge in and completely distract me, making it impossible to even focus on reading a book.
Can you estimate how much of your daily time is spent on these persistent 'what-ifs' and worst-case scenarios, is it more than an hour, a few hours, or almost the entire day?

It really feels like almost the entire day, starting from the moment I wake up and my mind begins hopping from one worry to the next. Even when I try to relax in the evening or attend my book club, those "what-ifs" just keep barging back in, making it feel completely constant.

Do you experience any periods of the day where you're able to fully disengage from these persistent 'what-ifs' and worst-case scenarios, or are they always present in the background, even when you're engaged in activities?

They are almost always present in the background, and it's incredibly difficult to disengage from them. Even when I try to distract myself with reading or my book club, the worries just barge back in. I often find I’ve reread the same page three times because my mind has wandered right back to those what-ifs.
